definitions.gloss: beat; the basic unit of musical time; counter for beats
definitions.explanation: The regular pulse that underlies a piece of music, and the counter used to count those pulses. In Japanese music theory it is the traditional term for the English 'beat.'

examples.japanese: ⟦{指揮者|しきしゃ}→指揮者：06565_shikisha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{拍|はく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧。
⟦{曲|きょく}→曲：09881_kyoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{拍|はく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{合|あ}わせて→合わせる：01872_awaseru⟧⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧たたく。
examples.english: I clap along to the beat of the song.

examples.japanese: ⟦{音楽|おんがく}→音楽：00661_ongaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{拍|はく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{正確|せいかく}→正確：03372_seikaku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{刻|きざ}む→刻む：03918_kizamu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{難|むずか}しい→難しい：00517_muzukashii⟧。
examples.english: Keeping the beat of music precisely is difficult.

notes:
The traditional term in Japanese music theory for a beat — the basic pulse of music — and the counter for counting beats (e.g. ⟦{二|に}→二：00736_ni⟧{拍|はく}, two beats). In casual and pop-music contexts the loanword ⟦ビート→ビート：06590_biito⟧ is more common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {拍|はく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧: to keep the beat
- {拍|はく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{合|あ}わせる→合わせる：01872_awaseru⟧: to match the beat
- ⟦{表|おもて}→表：01355_omote⟧{拍|はく}: the on-beat
- ⟦{裏|うら}→裏：02178_ura⟧{拍|はく}: the off-beat

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {拍子|びょうし}: time; meter — how beats are grouped (e.g. ⟦{三|さん}{拍子|びょうし}→三拍子：22260_sanbyoushi⟧, triple time)
- ⟦ビート→ビート：06590_biito⟧: beat — the everyday loanword, common in pop and rock
